speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance, size, and duration of the skin lesions you are concerned about? REQUEST TEST: Full body skin examination.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Inspection: An erythematous plaque with areas of crusting, oozing, and irregular borders observed on the dorsal surface of the penile shaft and on the left middle finger. Palpation: Lesions are firm to touch, non-tender, with no warmth. Regional Lymph Nodes: No palpable cervical, axillary, or inguinal lymphadenopathy. Biopsy Findings: Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium. STD Panel: Syphilis Negative, HIV Negative, HBV Negative, HCV Negative. Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), Blood Pressure 130/85 mmHg, Heart Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min.

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any changes in the borders of these lesions, such as becoming raised, rolled, or ulcerated, and have they appeared over a period of months rather than weeks? REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of penile and digital lesions.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The biopsy reveals cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium. STD Panel results are negative for Syphilis, HIV, HBV, and HCV. Vital signs are stable.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) of the penis and digit.
